name: RYMAN HOSPITALITY PROPERTIES REIT

priced.reason: not a repriceable fcff name or no growth supplied

devils_advocate.strongest_counter: The counter to a neutral qualitative note is that a specific, dated, financeable event just happened and it deserves a view. Ryman has taken pro-forma debt from roughly $3.97B toward $4.67B and issued 5.865M shares — about 7% of the pre-deal count — to buy two Orlando luxury resorts for $1.38B. That is a large, levered, late-cycle acquisition of TRANSIENT and leisure-luxury hotels by a company whose entire competitive advantage is the CONTRACTED GROUP model. Grande Lakes is a different business with a different demand curve, and it is exactly the kind of diversification that historically ends REIT re-ratings. The equity is also trading at $129.33 against the $117.00 the company just issued at, so the market has marked the deal up by 10% before a single quarter of ownership.
devils_advocate.what_would_prove_it: The Grande Lakes properties' group-versus-transient booking mix and their contribution to same-store metrics once they enter the comparable set, together with pro-forma net-debt-to-EBITDAre after a full year. If the Orlando assets dilute the forward booking visibility that justifies Ryman's premium, the multiple should compress regardless of how accretive the deal looks on day one.
devils_advocate.already_visible: No — and that is the honest answer rather than a comfortable one. The deal is three weeks old, the notes priced at 6.250% which is unremarkable rather than distressed, the equity raise cleared at a 9% discount to today's price, and the core business is putting up records with raised guidance. There is no visible stress. But there is also no data yet on how the acquired assets perform inside this portfolio, so the counter is unfalsified rather than refuted.
devils_advocate.unresolved: Whether $1.38B is the right price for the Grande Lakes assets, which I cannot judge without the purchase cap rate — it was not in any source I could reach, and I could not open the 2026-08-10 or 2026-08-25 8-Ks. Also unresolved: the Opry Entertainment separation, which is a real and potentially large source of value that is impossible to price while management says only that discussions continue and no agreement exists.

what_changed: The balance sheet changed materially in three weeks. Q2 2026 (2026-08-07): record revenue $749.0M (+13.6%), net income $102.1M, adjusted EBITDAre $258.3M, same-store RevPAR +5.2%, total RevPAR +6.5%, Entertainment revenue a record $144.0M; unrestricted cash of $366.1M and total debt of $3,969.5M net of unamortised deferred financing costs at 30 June; 2026 capex guided to $400-500M. Then on 2026-08-10 a subsidiary agreed to purchase the JW Marriott Orlando Grande Lakes and the Ritz-Carlton Orlando Grande Lakes plus related assets for approximately $1.38B. It was funded with 5,100,000 shares at $117.00 plus a fully exercised 765,000-share option — about $658M of net proceeds, closed 2026-08-12 — together with a private placement of $700M of 6.250% senior notes due 2035 raising roughly $689M net, plus cash on hand. On Opry Entertainment, discussions with select potential investors continue and management states no agreement has been entered into.
consensus_case: Ryman owns the Gaylord group-convention hotels — very large, self-contained meeting properties with a booking model that is nothing like transient lodging: group business is contracted years ahead, which gives unusual forward visibility into occupancy and rate, and the properties are effectively irreplaceable because nobody is building 2,000-room convention resorts at current construction costs. Q2 2026 was an all-time record: consolidated revenue $749.0M, up 13.6%, net income $102.1M, adjusted EBITDAre $258.3M. Same-store hospitality RevPAR rose 5.2% to about $202 and total RevPAR 6.5% to about $524, each roughly 2.5 points ahead of expectations, and management raised the same-store hospitality adjusted EBITDAre guidance midpoint by $10M while guiding low-to-mid single-digit RevPAR growth for Q3 and Q4. Alongside that sits a second business the market values separately: Opry Entertainment Group did a record $144.0M of quarterly revenue, and management continues to discuss a path to greater independence for it with potential outside investors — an unpriced separation option. The market is paying for contracted forward group revenue, an irreplaceable asset base, and that optionality.
key_risks: Leverage stepping from roughly $3.97B toward $4.67B to fund a $1.38B acquisition, alongside $400-500M of 2026 capex
Grande Lakes shifts mix toward transient and leisure-luxury, away from the contracted-group model that is the company's actual moat
About 7% share issuance at $117.00 against a $129.33 price — the deal is being marked up before any operating evidence
Group convention demand is a lagging cyclical: bookings are contracted years ahead, which cushions the downturn and delays the recovery equally
This engine has no defensible free model for REITs, so nothing here is a quantitative conclusion
watch_for: Grande Lakes performance and group-versus-transient mix once it enters the same-store set
Pro-forma net debt to adjusted EBITDAre after a full year of ownership
Any definitive agreement on an Opry Entertainment Group investment or separation — currently explicitly not agreed
Forward group booking pace, which is the leading indicator this business actually has
